fang_nzame.name: orders the heavenly bodies and sets the cosmos in motion
fang_nzame.notes: In the Beti-Pahuin (Fang/Bulu/Ewondo) triad Nzame governs the heavens and the celestial bodies while Mebere and Nkwa hold the male and female aspects of creation.

sources.reference: Talk Africana, 'The Creation Story of the Fang people of Africa'

fang_sekume.name: fashions his wife Mbongwe from a living tree
fang_sekume.notes: Created mortal (unlike the immortal but cursed Fam), Sekume is made the new progenitor of the Fang and forms his consort Mbongwe from a tree, becoming ancestor of the people.

sources.reference: Encyclopaedia of Fang creation myth (Nzame–Mebere–Nkwa cycle)

fang_nkwa.name: endows the first man Fam with beauty
fang_nkwa.notes: Third person of the creator triad, holding the beauty-aspect of creation: from Nkwa the first man Fam receives his beauty, as he takes strength from Nzame and leadership from Mebere.

sources.reference: Talk Africana, 'The Creation Story of the Fang people'

fijian_nacirikaumoli.name: shoots Degei's sacred cock Turukawa and provokes the first war
fijian_nacirikaumoli.notes: With his twin he kills Degei's wake-rooster Turukawa with a bow of Togovere mangrove, the killing that brings Degei's wrath and the first tribal war of the Nakauvadra.

sources.reference: Fiji Times, 'How tribal war started in Fiji'

fijian_nakausabaria.name: shoots Degei's sacred cock Turukawa and provokes the first war
fijian_nakausabaria.notes: With his twin he looses the mangrove arrow that slays Degei's rooster Turukawa, igniting the first tribal war in which Degei calls Vueti's warriors from Verata against them.

sources.reference: Fiji Times, 'How tribal war started in Fiji'

fijian_degei.name: judges the souls of the dead at his cave
fijian_degei.notes: At his cave on the summit of Uluda in the Nakauvadra range Degei meets the dead as their judge, determining their passage into the afterlife.

sources.reference: Williams, Fiji and the Fijians (1858); Bula Living, 'Degei: The Supreme God'

fijian_dakuwaqa.name: changes shape between man and great shark
fijian_dakuwaqa.notes: His true form is a muscular Fijian man with a shark's upper torso; he ranges the islands fighting the other reef-guardians.

sources.reference: Fiji Times, 'The birth and home of the shark god Dakuwaqa'

fijian_ratumaibulu.name: makes the breadfruit and fruit-trees blossom and bear
fijian_ratumaibulu.notes: In the lunar month Vula-i-Ratumaibulu he ascends from Bulu (the spirit-world) to inspect and bless the land so the trees flower and fruit.

fijian_rokola.name: masters the building of the great voyaging canoes
fijian_rokola.notes: Head craftsman of the matai (carpenter caste); builds the Kaunitoni and, at Degei's order, the new canoes that carry the ancestors eastward.

sources.reference: Godchecker, 'Rokola'; Popular Science Monthly vol. 47 (1895), 'Ancestor Worship Among the Fijians'

finnish_ahti.name: rules the water-realm Ahtola and its hundred sea-caves
finnish_ahti.notes: Styled 'master of the billows, ruler over a hundred sea-caves'; he and Vellamo dwell at the bottom of the sea in the chasms of the salmon-rocks.

sources.reference: Kalevala (Lönnrot), fishing runos; Crawford trans. preface

finnish_ahti.name: drives the fish and grants the catch to fishers and seal-hunters
finnish_ahti.notes: As giver of the deep's bounty he is invoked to send fish into the nets and ensure success in fishing and sealing.

finnish_ilmatar.name: descends from the air to float on the primal sea for ages
finnish_ilmatar.notes: Lonely in the celestial air she descends to the shoreless waters and floats there for centuries until the world is made on her body.

finnish_mielikki.name: keeps the keys of Tapiola's storehouses and looses the game
finnish_mielikki.notes: As Mistress of the Forest she holds the keys to the wood's treasures and releases game to favoured hunters.

finnish_mielikki.name: heals trapped and wounded forest creatures and knows the healing herbs
finnish_mielikki.notes: She mends animals caught in snares, heals fallen chicks and worn grouse, and is mistress of the curative plants of the wood.

finnish_tapio.name: hosts hunters as lord of Tapiola and opens the forest's stores
finnish_tapio.notes: As 'master of the forest' he must be entreated with prayer and offering at the wood's edge before a hunter may take its game.

finnish_pellervoinen.name: sows the trees, fields, marshes and all vegetation of the earth
finnish_pellervoinen.notes: At Väinämöinen's bidding the slender youth scatters seed across the new land — firs on the mountains, pines on the hills, birches in the marshes, alders in loose soil — until the forests rise.

finnish_pekko.name: ripens the barley and quickens the fermenting of beer
finnish_pekko.notes: God of barley and brewing among the Finns and the Seto; he makes the grain grow in the field and the malt ferment in the vat.

sources.reference: Mikael Agricola, deity list (1551); Seto Peko tradition

finnish_tuoni.name: receives all souls into Tuonela across the death-river
finnish_tuoni.notes: He is no punisher but the inevitable lord into whose realm every soul comes; the dead must cross the river of Tuoni to reach his hall.

finnish_tuonetar.name: serves new-come souls the ale of oblivion that wipes the memory of life
finnish_tuonetar.notes: Queen of Tuonela, she welcomes the dead with the beer of forgetfulness so that they remember nothing of the living world.

finnish_lempo.name: turns the axe aside to wound the woodsman
finnish_lempo.notes: With Hiisi he twists Väinämöinen's hatchet from its stroke so that it gashes the sage's knee (Runo 8), the type-case of his power to spoil tools and deeds.

finnish_aino.name: drowns and becomes a maiden of Vellamo, taking salmon-form
finnish_aino.notes: Rather than wed the old sage she walks into the lake and drowns, passing to the home of the water-maidens in Vellamo's realm; thereafter she swims as a salmon and slips, mocking, from Väinämöinen's hands (Runos 4–5).

sources.reference: Kalevala (Lönnrot), Runo 4 (The Fate of Aino), Runo 5

fon_dan.name: carries the creator Mawu-Lisa in his mouth while the earth is shaped
fon_dan.notes: The cosmic serpent bears Mawu-Lisa about as the world is formed, then coils beneath the earth to hold everything in place.

sources.reference: Herskovits, Dahomey: An Ancient West African Kingdom (1938); Oxford Reference, 'Aido-Hwedo'

fon_dan.name: revolves about the earth and moves the heavenly bodies
fon_dan.notes: Encircling the world, his revolution causes the movement of sun, moon and stars; his visible track is the rainbow.

fon_gu.name: brings the knowledge of iron-working to humankind
fon_gu.notes: Fifth-born of Mawu-Lisa and tool of the creator, Gu is the means by which blacksmithing and the working of metal were given to people.

fon_gu.name: empowers warriors and clears the way of obstacles
fon_gu.notes: Vodun of war and patron of soldiers; offerings were made before his iron image to release force before battle and to protect against enemies.

fon_sogbo.name: brings the fertilizing rain along with thunder and lightning
fon_sogbo.notes: Beyond hurling the bolt, the thunder-vodun gives the rain that makes the fields fertile, uniting destruction (lightning) and life (rain).

fon_sogbo.name: smites liars, thieves, witches and the wicked with the thunderbolt
fon_sogbo.notes: As enforcer of justice he strikes down evildoers with his lightning, chastising the false and the criminal.

fon_sakpata.name: gives the life-bringing rain and the fertility of the soil
fon_sakpata.notes: As lord of the earth he is god of agriculture, mastering the fertile ground and the rain that feeds the crops.

fon_nana_buluku.name: brings forth the twin creator Mawu-Lisa, the moon and the sun
fon_nana_buluku.notes: The primordial androgyne older than the world originates the universe and gives birth to Mawu (moon) and Lisa (sun), to whom the ordering of creation passes.

ga_ataa_naa_nyongmo.name: sends famine or abundance by withholding or granting the rains
ga_ataa_naa_nyongmo.notes: The Ga remember a great famine ended when Ataa-Naa Nyɔŋmɔ answered libations with a deluge of rain; he both starves and feeds the people through the weather, the memory mocked-and-thanked at Homowo.

sources.reference: Osabu-Kle, 'The Ga People and Homowo Festival' (Carleton Univ.)

ga_kpele.name: possess priests and mediums to speak with the living
ga_kpele.notes: The dzemawɔdzi descend upon individuals, making them wɔŋtsɛmɛi/woyei (mediums) and wulɔmɔi (priests) through whom the gods communicate; named members include Osabu, Dantu, La-Kpa and the lagoon-gods.

sources.reference: Kilson, Kpele Lala: Ga Religious Songs and Symbols (1971)

sources.reference: Talk Africana, 'The Creation Story of the Fang people'

sources.reference: Fiji Times, 'Beqa, divers and Dakuwaqa the shark god'

sources.reference: Ancient Origins, 'The Creation Myth of Fiji and the Serpent God'

sources.reference: Oxford Reference, 'Aido-Hwedo'; The Circle of the Dragon, 'Aido Hwedo'

fijian_dakuwaqa.name: Pouring of yaqona to the shark-god
fijian_dakuwaqa.notes: Fishermen reverently pour a bowl of yaqona (kava) into the sea for Dakuwaqa so that he will guard their canoes through the reef-passages; the chiefs of Cakaudrove are reckoned his descendants and his totem-shark appears to the reigning Tui Cakau before momentous news.

sources.reference: Fiji Times, 'Beqa, divers and Dakuwaqa the shark god'

fijian_degei.name: First bowl of yaqona dedicated to Degei
fijian_degei.notes: In the yaqona (kava) ceremony the first bowl poured is committed to Degei as the highest honour; his cave on Uluda in the Nakauvadra range is held tabu sara (utterly sacred).

sources.reference: Mythlok, 'Degei'; Ancient Origins, 'The Creation Myth of Fiji'

fijian_cagawalu.name: War-temple cult of Bau (Vatanitawake)
fijian_cagawalu.notes: The war-god of Bau was served in the bure kalou; his temple at Vatanitawake (rebuilt by Tanoa and Cakobau, burned 1854) was where the bete (priests) were consulted before the island went to war. A missionary in 1866 noted a 'new god' Cagawalu worshipped 'to proclaim and accomplish a new dynasty'.

sources.reference: Fiji Times, 'Bau Island's Vatanitawake'; Learning About the World, 'Fiji – Gods of War'

fijian_ravuravu.name: Rock-eating rite of Ravuravu's priests
fijian_ravuravu.notes: The priests of the murder-god were said to consume stones to commune with him and gain supernatural power; sitting on a rock he had sat upon, or treading his footprints, was believed to turn a person whiter than an albino.

sources.reference: Old World Gods, 'Ravuravu'; Glitternight, 'Gods and Goddesses of Fiji'

finnish_ukko.name: Ukko's vakkas (the spring sacrifice)
finnish_ukko.cadence: in May, at the spring sowing
finnish_ukko.notes: The vakkajuhlat were held at sowing-time in the community's sacred grove (hiisi): a vessel (vakka) of ale or food was offered, sometimes with an animal sacrifice, to secure good weather and a good harvest. Recorded by the reformer Mikael Agricola in his list of Finnish 'idolatry'.

sources.reference: Mikael Agricola, preface to the Psalter (1551)

finnish_pekko.name: The autumn Peko feast
finnish_pekko.notes: Among the Seto a wax-and-wood image of Peko, kept the year round in the grain-bin, was brought out for a men's feast of eating and drinking; the men chanted 'Peko, Peko, come to drink the beer', the elders acting as his priests and making the sacrifice. Before Pentecost young men fought until first blood, the bleeder hosting next year's feast.

fon_sogbo.name: Hevioso thunder-cult with the ritual axe
fon_sogbo.notes: Initiates of the thunder-vodun bear the crescent-bladed ritual axe (sɔ-kpɛn) in dances and ceremonies; the ram is sacrificed and the colours red and fire belong to the cult.

fon_sakpata.name: Sakpata dance of thanksgiving for rain
fon_sakpata.notes: Vodun followers gather to dance for Sakpata in thanks after rain; from him issues the cult of smallpox, which held that the god punished wrongdoing through the disease.

fon_mawu_lisa.name: Cult of Mawu-Lisa at Abomey
fon_mawu_lisa.notes: The cult of Mawu-Lisa was centred at Abomey, the Dahomey capital; the priests of Mawu wear white, and a rare statue at Abomey shows the figure painted red with large breasts, holding a crescent moon.

sources.reference: Herskovits, Dahomey: An Ancient West African Kingdom (1938)

fon_legba.name: Legba shrine at the threshold
fon_legba.cadence: daily, before approaching the other vodun
fon_legba.notes: An unfired earthen mound bearing a wooden or iron phallus is set at the village gate or house-door; as keeper of every threshold Legba must be addressed first, for only through him can the other vodun be reached, and earthen phallic figures were driven into the soil to stir agricultural fertility.

sources.reference: Herskovits, Dahomey (1938); Oriire, 'Before You Pray, Ask Legba'

fon_dan.name: Python cult of Dangbe (Ouidah)
fon_dan.cadence: continuous tendance of the sacred pythons
fon_dan.notes: The serpent-vodun is venerated in the Temple of Pythons at Ouidah, where living royal pythons are kept and tended as embodiments of Dan/Dangbe.

ga_ataa_naa_nyongmo.name: Homowo libations to the supreme being
ga_ataa_naa_nyongmo.notes: At Homowo ('hooting at hunger') the Ga pour libations to Ataa-Naa Nyɔŋmɔ, the dzemawɔdzi and the ancestors at planting and harvest to ensure abundance, commemorating the famine the supreme being ended with rain; the high god is rarely approached directly, the lesser gods serving as intermediaries.

sources.reference: Osabu-Kle, 'The Ga People and Homowo Festival' (Carleton Univ.)

ga_kpele.name: The kpele cult and its dancing
ga_kpele.cadence: at Homowo and on cult occasions
ga_kpele.notes: The dzemawɔdzi (kpele gods) are served in the kpele cult of central Accra: drum-accompanied kpele songs (kpele lala) call them down to possess mediums, and the kpele dance follows the Homowo feast by day.

sources.reference: Kilson, Kpele Lala (1971); Dancing with the Gods (2013)

attributes.name: man with a shark's upper torso
attributes.notes: His true form is a powerfully built Fijian man whose upper body is that of a great shark; he can take any shape but reverts to the shark.

sources.reference: Fiji Times, 'The birth and home of the shark god Dakuwaqa'

attributes.name: colossal serpent coiled in the mountain cave
attributes.notes: Degei is enshrined as an immense snake whose turning in his Nakauvadra cave is felt as earthquakes.

sources.reference: Ferrebeekeeper, 'Degei, the Serpent God of Fiji'

attributes.name: lighted reeds bound to his head
attributes.notes: His mother bound burning reeds to his head so he could be seen at night; the phosphorescence of his passing names him 'expert of light'.

sacredAnimals.name: the waterfowl (scaup/duck) that nests on her knee

attributes.name: gold breast-cross and silver ornaments laid aside at the shore
attributes.notes: Before drowning she takes off her gold cross, rings, ribbons and silken dress on the lakeside rock — the image fixed in Gallen-Kallela's Aino triptych (1891).

attributes.name: the paired standing-stones of the twins in the Nakauvadra range
attributes.notes: Two ancient stones in the Rakiraki highlands are pointed out as representing Cirinakaumoli and Nakausabaria of pre-Christian Fiji.

sources.reference: Fiji Times / oral tradition of the Nakauvadra twin-stones

attributes.name: moss coat, lichen beard and fir-leaf hat
attributes.notes: A tall, slender figure clad in tree-moss, with a beard of lichen, brows of moss and a high fir-needle hat — a Green-Man of the wood.

sacredAnimals.name: the bear (Otso), king of the forest

sources.reference: Wikipedia, 'Ukko' (rowan as Ukko's sacred tree, via Rauni)

attributes.name: red-painted figure with large breasts holding a crescent moon
attributes.notes: The rare cult image at Abomey is painted red, with large breasts, holding the crescent of Mawu the moon; her priests wear white.

attributes.name: the double-headed (crescent) thunder-axe
attributes.notes: The twin crescent blades are his central emblem — one side destruction and fiery judgment (lightning), the other restoration and life (rain).

sources.reference: Wikipedia, 'Xevioso' (the ram, colour red and fire)

attributes.name: the red, white and black spots of smallpox
attributes.notes: Sakpata is marked by black, white and red spots and bears the 'arm of smallpox', scissors and chain; his colours are red, black and white.

attributes.name: the coiled rainbow-serpent biting its tail
attributes.notes: A vast serpent whose body is the rainbow, encircling and supporting the world and devouring its own tail when iron runs short.

sources.reference: The Circle of the Dragon, 'Aido Hwedo'; Oxford Reference, 'Aido-Hwedo'
Mythlok, 'Temple of Pythons' (royal pythons of Dangbe)

attributes.name: earthen mound bearing an exaggerated phallus
attributes.notes: Legba is figured as a phallus or a man with an outsized phallus, his shrine an unfired earthen mound at the gate.

sources.reference: Herskovits, Dahomey (1938); Erotic Heritage Museum, 'Legba and the Fon People'
Oriire, 'Before You Pray, Ask Legba' (dog among his symbols)

sacredAnimals.name: the elephant, leopard and monkey first set over the earth

sources.reference: Talk Africana, 'The Creation Story of the Fang people'
